AllocTheme: An allocation that addresses the most urgent winterization and critical and life-saving gaps in the response to COVID-19 in North West Syria. The allocation covers all humanitarian sectors with 17.6 million USD.
AllocSummary: This standard allocation aims to address two specific objectives: critical and life-saving gaps in the response to COVID-19 and the most urgent winterization needs of people, prioritizing underserved and high-needs areas. Considering the large amount of funding allocated by the SCHF during 2020 (US$166 million) and the limited funding available under this allocation, priority will be given to projects with strong emphasis on critical life-saving interventions that directly link with the allocation objectives. This allocation will call for strong integration and complementarity to ensure an efficient coverage of and response to emergency needs. These strategic objectives aim to provide timely seasonal assistance and support the continuity of essential life-saving interventions for vulnerable people in northwest Syria affected by displacement and in places of origin in cases where people have returned. Considering the approaching winter season and COVID-19 pandemic, projects with an ability to start implementation immediately will be prioritized, conditional on having a strong risk management in place and a robust strategy to ensure accountability to the affected population throughout the project cycle. Winterization assistance funded under this allocation will take a people-centred approach including ensuring community and individuals are wholly addressed. The prioritized list of activities has been listed in the section below. COVID-19 sensitive programming should be applied across the projects implemented under the different sectors and should become a part of regular programming. During the allocation process, final decisions on RCCE-related interventions will also include a review and evaluation from a representative of the relevant clusters. Interventions will be implemented according to cluster guidance and international humanitarian standards. New working modalities that include remote services and adjusted activities due to COVID-19 are supported and encouraged. Geographical locations prioritized under this allocation are in line with the most recent needs assessments, critical gaps and overburdened communities' analysis and clusters’ inputs. The allocation decision-making process will review locations prioritized in each and across clusters to ensure complementarity and avoid duplications, including with previous SCHF allocations. Interventions targeting high-needs and underserved areas in complementarity with other activities on the ground will be prioritized. The maximum duration possible is 12 months for projects funded under this allocation. Projects contributing to winterization should start as soon as possible and demonstrate a feasible and realistic implementation plan. Winterization projects should start distribution as soon as possible upon budget clearance to ensure a timely delivery of aid. Project funded under this allocation must demonstrate strong cost-efficiency, taking into consideration currency fluctuation, market prices and, where applicable, other ongoing projects funded by SCHF including already funded support costs. The budgets submitted must demonstrate coherence and relevance of the logical framework, proposed activities, and value for money.
AllocLocation: All projects location are in Idleb and Aleppo Governorates, North West Syria.

AllocTheme: Standard Allocation to support prioritized activities of the 2020 Humanitarian Response Plan that also contribute to the rapidly scaled-up COVID-19 prevention and response in Iraq.

Some $11.2 million out of the total allocation of $12.3 million funds the COVID-19 addendum to the 2020 HRP. The IHF through this allocation is continuously pursuing the consortium approach aimed at enhancing the participation and response capacity of national partners; through this approach, a net funding of $3.6 million (30 per cent of the total allocation) is disbursed to national NGOs. The allocation funds 20 projects implemented by 42 partners including 20 international NGOs, 16 national NGOs, 5 UN agencies and 1 Red Cross/Red Crescent organization. At least 1.2 million people are targeted with humanitarian assistance.

Under the 2020 Cost Extensions strategy, approved on 29 October, the IHF cost-extended 18 cluster-recommended projects funded through the 2020 1st Standard Allocation and 2019 2nd Standard Allocation. These cost extensions allowed for quick disbursement of funds with minimum processing time and extra work for clusters and partners to support the expanded operation of already-formed consortia in Education, Food Security, Health, MPCA, Protection, Shelter/NFIs and WASH sectors, addressing critical operational and funding gaps in the 2020 HRP. Part of these cost extensions also supported COVID-19 response.

AllocTheme: An allocation that addresses a spectrum of needs following massive displacement of 840,000 people in North West Syria and following the ceasefire of March 6, 2020. The allocation covers all humanitarian sectors with 75 million USD.
AllocSummary:
While displacement becomes more protracted, needs with longer-term impacts are increasing in prominence; this standard allocation aims to address both these sets of needs through immediate and slightly longer-term interventions to respond to high vulnerability level of a large part of the population living in northwest Syria. In doing so, it will also focus on strengthening elements of the preparedness and response to the COVID-19 pandemic as well as to adapt the response modalities to ensure the continuation and expansion of the humanitarian response.
The allocation will focus on the continuity of essential life-saving services and efforts to ensure dignified living conditions for the most vulnerable people in northwest Syria in both place of displacement, and in places of origin in cases where people have returned. Interventions will be prioritized based on the most recent needs assessments while ensuring the integration of doing no harm principles to mitigate vulnerabilities and build some element of sustainability into certain services such as WASH and Education. This allocation is also forward-thinking with the inclusion of winterization plans. These will start in August, given the lead times on the administrative and procurement processes. 
The latest HNAP assessment conducted in March 2020 reported the priority needs are shelter (63%), basic services (59%) and food (55%). Accordingly, this allocation will align its response to meet these needs and ensure the continuation of basic services prioritizing most vulnerable people and have a strong emphasis on women and girls, people with disabilities and older persons and protection.
The allocation supports integration across all the clusters to better address needs and provide a comprehensive response. It strives to enhance coordination and collaboration between clusters and partners, and aspires to be more than just the simple inclusion of multiple cluster elements within a project, but rather support an integrated approach that combines mutually supportive programme elements, either within a single cluster or a multi-cluster, to achieve a common result. For example, for the establishment of new camps, WASH, CCM and S/NFI clusters will coordinate form very early planning stages to ensure that comprehensive services are provided. 
Information on the humanitarian situation in northwest Syria is difficult to obtain, and access to affected communities remains the main challenge. The frequency and quality of current information flow are not consistent, while there are many sources of information are only accessible from the ground. This allocation will also support relevant common service that supports the wider humanitarian community.
In this context of increased uncertainty caused by several factors, the allocation will prioritize interventions factoring inflexible and responsible programming to rapidly adapt to changes to continue the provision of adequate basic services. The OCHA Humanitarian Financing team will continue working closely with partners to reprogramme should the need arise. Prioritized projects will propose a suitable risk management plan with a clear identification of internal and external risks and mitigation measures.
Interventions will be implemented according to cluster guidance and international humanitarian standards. New working modalities that include remote services and adjusted activities due to COVID-19 are supported and encouraged. Proposed interventions will be complementary to other SCHF ongoing projects (from the reserve, standard and COVID-19 allocations) and CERF grants, including the SCHF funding allocated at the beginning of the year to support the emergency response through the funding of the Preparedness and Response Plan for North West Syria issued in October 2019.
AllocLocation: All locations with particular focus on the camps are and new informal settlements in Aleppo and Idlib

AllocTheme:
In the two months since the detection of the first case of COVID-19 in Ukraine on 29 February, the number of cases is rising exponentially across the country, reaching 11,913 on 3 May. In the non-Government controlled areas (NGCA), 233 cases have been reported, but the actual figure is likely much higher due to insufficient capacity for testing and referrals. The people living in areas beyond government control in Donetska and Luhanska oblasts are at particular risk from the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic due to several pre-existing factors that are compounded by restrictions imposed to contain the virus.

First, the healthcare systems in NGCA have significantly been weakened due to the cumulative impact of years of armed conflict. Second, the economic contraction caused by years of conflict and the relatively elderly population (36 per cent compared to 23 per cent nationally) has increased the vulnerability of the NGCA population. Prior to the imposition of measures to control the spread of COVID-19, some 463,000 people crossed the ‘contact line’ each month from NGCA to access basic services, banking and pensions in Government-controlled areas (GCA). According to the 2019 multi-sector needs assessment, food was already the primary household expense prior to COVID-19. 

There is also a significant lack of information about that changing context in NGCA, and in general there has been much less information available and needs analysis on the humanitarian situation in NGCA compared to GCA. Therefore, this allocation will also support needs analysis in NGCA to assess the context around COVID-19 and a multisector and thematic needs assessment to enable evidence-based humanitarian aid delivery and planning in NGCA.
AllocSummary: The allocation will therefore provide $1.75 million to support elderly and other most vulnerable people with life-saving supplies and assistance,  provide support to the healthcare system and needs assessments in NGCA to mitigate the impact of COVID-19. All interventions will be implemented within appropriate do-no harm practices.
AllocLocation: The COVID-19 allocation will support partners who are established in NGCA and have the capacity, and operational readiness to begin projects immediately.
AllocTitle: UHF COVID-19 Allocation for Non-Government Controlled Areas of Eastern Ukraine

AllocTheme: Support to Sudan Country Preparedness and Response Plan (CPRP) for COVID-19.
AllocSummary:
The Humanitarian Country Team (HCT) and UN Country Team (UNCT) has developed a COVID-19 Country Preparedness and Response Plan (CPRP) based on the eight pillars outlined in the WHO guidance document (“Operational planning guidelines to support country preparedness and response”) which is also aligned to the FMOH COVID-19 plan.  The plan is to support the government of Sudan in their effort with a total requirements USD $87 million. The plan is built around the eight pillars focused on the major areas of the public health preparedness and response: (i) Country-level coordination, (ii) Points of entry (iii) Surveillance, rapid-response teams, and case investigation (iv) National laboratories (v) Case management (vi) Risk communication and community engagement, (vii) Infection prevention and control IPC, (viii) Operational support and Logistics. 

On 27 April, OCHA launched Reserve for Emergency to support CPRP with a total budget $10.5million. This allocation is focusing on 3 pillars of the CPRP: risk communication, infection prevention and control and case management. Four UN agencies and 12 NGO partners will be working in at least 16 states. About 60% of the budget is channeled to NGO partners. In addition on 20 March, SHF has also granted WHO with a budget of 495,247.47 to scaling up country preparedness to prevent imminent risk of importation, isolate and contain imported cases and prevent local spread of Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) in Sudan.
AllocLocation: Abiyei, Khartoum, North Darfur, South Darfur, Central Darfur, West Darfur, East Darfur, South Kordofan, West Kordofan, Blue Nile, White Nila, Red Sea, Kasala, Gezira, River Nile and Gadaref.
AllocTitle: Support to Sudan Country Preparedness and Response Plan (CPRP) -  Covid-19

AllocTheme: COVID 19 allocation
AllocSummary:
The allocation serves to foster preparedness to the COVID 19 pandemic to reinforce the Syria public health system and improve health awareness and preventative mechanisms.

The preparedness and response planning for COVID 19 will be focused on reinforcing comprehensive, multi-sectoral preparedness and mitigation measures to prevent further transmission. At the same time, the allocation will also focus on protecting, assisting and advocating for the most vulnerable, including IDPs, refugees and Palestine refugees and host communities particularly vulnerable to the pandemic. Due to the many unknown factors about this new virus, it has been challenging to provide accurate predictions of the case in Syria. Based on the epidemiological pattern and modelling of COVID-19 in other countries, the current action is for immediate critical activities to be implemented in the next three to a maximum of six months. 

The allocation shall be provided to partners, with full flexibility in geographic coverage while maintaining emphasis on a needs-based coordinated response. Guided by the global preparedness and response to COVID-19 as well as the operational plan being developed by the inter-sector coordination, five main priorities are identified:
1)	Enhancement of surveillance capacity with a critical need to expand laboratory capacity to test for timely detection; and support case management and contact tracing
2)	Ensure infection prevention and control in healthcare facilities to protect health care workers from infection by COVID-19 and amplification of events in the healthcare facilities and communities
3)	Risk mitigation and community engagement through awareness raising and risk communication
4)	Address immediate gaps in logistics and transportation for humanitarian programming due to access restrictions  
5)	Protection of the most vulnerable population such, the elderly, women-headed household and people with disabilities, refugees. 

As per the COVID-19 Operational Response Plan, the response to the COVID-19 outbreak must be multi-sectoral in nature to be effective. The following sectors will be covered: Health, WASH, Protection and Logistics. The health sector will take on procurement of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) on behalf of the Health sector for humanitarian community.

AllocTheme: 2020 Reserve Allocation responding to COVID-19 outbreak.
AllocSummary:
Le Coordonnateur Humanitaire (CH) a approuvé une Allocation Reserve de 10 millions de dollars américains du FHRDC en vue de démarrer la réponse en complémentarité à toutes les interventions de réponse et prévention déjà en cours pour soutenir le Plan de Réponse multi-secteur d’urgence, qui constitue un addendum au Plan de Réponse Humanitaire 2020, spécifique à la réponse COVID-19, afin de s’assurer que effets de la pandémie soient pris en compte par les partenaires humanitaires en plus des besoins humanitaires existants. 

La priorité de cette allocation est donnée aux activités plus critiques dans le temps (time-critical) des trois Clusters clé, soit Santé, EHA et Protection inscrits dans le cadre de l’Objectif Stratégique 1 du Plan de Réponse, soit :

1.	Renforcer les activités EHA et les mesures de prévention et contrôle des infections dans les structures de santé et dans la communauté ; 
2.	Renforcer la communication et l'engagement communautaire pour réduire le risque de transmission du COVID-19 ; et
3.	Renforcer la détection des cas suspects de COVID-19 à travers la surveillance et les tests laboratoire.

A ce jour, cinq provinces (Kinshasa, Sud-Kivu, Nord-Kivu, Ituri et Kwilu) sont affectées. Les projets pourront intervenir sur les zones de santé les plus densement peuplées et socioéconomiquement défavorisées des dites provinces, de préférence prenant en compte les problématiques prioritaires de manière intégrée, multisectorielle.

L’Allocation Reserve (AR) est une modalité d’allocation destinée à l’allocation rapide et flexible des fonds en réponse à des circonstances imprévues, d’urgence ou à d’autres besoins pertinents selon le contexte. 

Dans ces circonstances exceptionnelles de cette intervention, et en accord avec le Manuel Opérationnel du FH RDC, le CH a décidé, en consultation avec le CC, d’adopter le processus à concurrence limitée. 

En conséquence, en consultation avec les coordonnateurs des clusters et d’autres forums de coordination, une liste de partenaires ont été pré-identifiés par l’UFH.

The allocation will target the most isolated communities along the conflict line in the government controlled areas of Eastern Ukraine. 
The risk of rapid local transmission is high and the people living in areas affected by the conflict on the government-controlled side of the “contact line” are particularly at risk to COVID-19 as there is a high proportion of elderly people (36) and the healthcare system has been badly affected by the cumulative impact of years of armed conflict.

AllocTheme:
On 30 January 2020, the WHO Director-General declared the COVID-19 outbreak a “public health emergency of international concern” (PHEIC). The Emergency Committee has also provided recommendations to WHO, to all countries, and to the global community, on measures to control the outbreak. On the 11 March 2020, WHO announced the COVID-19 outbreak a pandemic, affecting 123 countries and territories.  On 5 March, the Ministry of Health (MoH) of the occupied Palestinian territory (oPt) reported it's first seven confirmed COVID-19 cases to WHO - a cluster of hotel workers in Bethlehem who were in contact with a Greek tourist group which tested positive for COVID-19 upon their return to Greece. Since then, MoH reported 37 more confirmed cases bringing the total number to 44 (as of 18-Mar-2020, 10:00 am). Cases have now been reported in Bethlehem, Tulkarm, Nablus and Ramallah. The MoH has also reported the community transmission of the virus as family members of the first detected had also been tested positive for COVID-19.

Since the first cases were reported globally, the WHO office in the occupied Palestinian territory (oPt) and partners have been gradually expanding the support to the Palestinian Authority’s Ministry of Health (MoH) to prepare for and respond to the COVID-19 outbreak. These efforts intensified since the first reported cases in oPt. The overall objective of this project is to support the Palestinian Authority Ministry of Health (PA MoH) to stop the human-to-human transmission of the COVID-19 and provide adequate care for patients affected by COVID-19, their families and close contacts. The project aims to accelerate the strengthening and scaling-up of the MoH capacity to prevent, early detect and respond to COVID-19 outbreak. WHO will support the MoH in: (1) procuring and delivering the PPE supplies, (2) supporting MoH's efforts in scaling-up COVID-19 case management, especially in Gaza focussing on ensuring the ability of the health system to treat COVID-19 cases, including critical ones, and expanding laboratory support. As part of the inter-agency risk communication and community engagement task force, WHO will support collective efforts to educate and actively communicate with the public and reaching the population with tailored messaging through community engagement and interpersonal communication approaches. WHO estimates that up to 5,000 women and men in OpT will have access to adequate COVID-19 treatment, up to 600 patients will have COVID-19 tests and communities in all 5 Gaza governorates will have received communication messages for prevention of COVID-19 (up to 500,000 men and women). Additionally, up to 500 health workers will benefit from capacity-building activities, and up to 65 health facilities will benefit from infection prevention and control supplies.

The allocation’s objective is to provide resources to address priority humanitarian needs in alignment with the 2019 HRP strategic objectives. The allocation will prioritise front-line activities based on their relative time-criticality and an understanding of funding available from other sources.
The allocation will prioritize about 26 counites that have been identified as priority based on the inter-sectoral severity of need analysis. The counites were selected through the ICWG consultations and took into account the inter-sectoral severity of need and gaps humanitarian response.

AllocTheme: Cash assistance in response to rising food insecurity (20-RR-WFP-054)
AllocSummary: The food security situation in South Sudan remains worrying. The drivers of food insecurity are due to the impact of the floods that affected close to a million people mainly along the Nile river that has affected harvests; the conflict that has affected access to livelihoods and is expected to continue during the dry season; the macro-economic conditions in the country; the high food prices; and the recurring high food insecurity over the years leading to asset stripping and negative coping mechanisms. For this CERF allocation, WFP will use unrestricted cash to respond to rising food insecurity to allow affected people to meet their food needs. The cash assistance from this CERF funding will be prioritised for households with a high risk to food, nutrition and protection-related vulnerabilities, including (but not limited to) female-headed households, households headed by persons with disabilities and child-headed households. The assistance will support alleviation of immediate food needs for 153,969 people. WFP will respond with in-kind assistance using funds from other donors to cover immediate food needs, where cash assistance is not possible. AllocTheme: Mitigating and Responding to the COVID-2019 Outbreak in humanitarian settings
AllocSummary: The main objective of this project is to provide life-saving health care and protection assistance in response to sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV) in 8 countries: Afghanistan, Burkina Faso, Chad, Haiti, the occupied Palestinian territory, South Sudan, Sudan and Venezuela. This UNFPA project provides essential sexual and reproductive health medical supplies; provides equipment and material for infection prevention and control (including personal protective equipment); ensures safe delivery and access to emergency obstetric and newborn care, clinical management of rape, psychosocial support services, family planning services and availability of contraceptives; provides life-saving SGBV services including medical, psychosocial support and SGBV case management; ensures the continuity of supplies, medicines and care for life-saving sexual and reproductive health services; and supports risk communication and community engagement towards primary prevention, contact tracing and stigma reduction.
AllocLocation: UNFPA will implement activities in Burkina Faso
AllocTitle: UNFPA: Mitigating and Responding to the COVID-2019 Outbreak in humanitarian settings (20-RR-FPA-022)

AllocTheme: Early action response to global containment of Novel Coronavirus outbreak
AllocSummary: The main objective of this project is to provide timely life-saving health assistance in priority countries in order to contain the global outbreak of the COVID-19 virus. This WHO project focuses on the 8 pillars of WHO's Strategic Preparedness and Response Plan, namely: (i) country-level coordination and monitoring; (ii) risk communication and community engagement; (iii) surveillance, rapid response teams, and case investigation; (iv) points of entry; (v) national laboratories; (vi) infection prevention and control; (vii) case management; and (viii) operational support and logistics. CERF funds will be used to focus on countries with imported cases or that are at high risk of imported cases and have limited operational response capacity.
AllocLocation: WHO will implement COVID response activities in Sudan.
